classification.difficultyReason: Students must introduce auxiliary parallels through the bends and combine transferred angles symbolically. The numerical and matching symbolic diagrams scaffold the final configuration, which also requires a supplementary angle.

spec.description: Horizontal parallel lines and an intervening three-segment zigzag.
spec.mathematics: Upper angle 20°, left bend alpha, right bend 50°, lower angle 30°.

answer.worked:
Draw a horizontal line through the left bend, parallel to the two given lines. Let $x$ be the angle below this line between it and the middle segment. Transfer the lower $30^\circ$ angle to a horizontal line through the right bend using corresponding angles.
$$\begin{align*}x&=50^\circ-30^\circ\\x&=20^\circ\\\alpha&=20^\circ+x\\\alpha&=40^\circ\end{align*}$$
The upper $20^\circ$ transfers to the left bend by alternate angles.

spec.description: Two horizontal parallel lines with a three-segment zigzag between them.
spec.mathematics: Theta is the upper angle, alpha the left bend, gamma the right bend and beta the lower angle.

answer.short:
$\alpha=\theta+(\gamma-\beta)$.

Use auxiliary lines parallel to the two given lines.
answer.worked:
Draw horizontal lines through the two interior bends, parallel to the given lines. Let $x$ be the angle between the middle segment and a horizontal line. Corresponding angles transfer $\beta$ to the right bend, and alternate angles transfer $\theta$ to the left bend.
$$\begin{align*}x&=\gamma-\beta\\\alpha&=\theta+x\\\alpha&=\theta+(\gamma-\beta)\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Parallel horizontal lines joined by a broken line with an obtuse alpha at its first bend.
spec.mathematics: Theta is below the upper line; alpha is above the first bend; beta is at the right vertex; gamma is above the lower line.

answer.short:
$\alpha=(180^\circ-\theta)+(\beta-\gamma)$.

Use a straight angle and auxiliary parallel lines.
answer.worked:
Draw horizontal lines through the two interior bends, parallel to the given lines. Let $x$ be the angle between the middle segment and a horizontal line. At the right vertex, corresponding angles give $\beta=x+\gamma$. At the first bend, the angle from the upper-left segment to the rightward horizontal ray is $180^\circ-\theta$.
$$\begin{align*}x&=\beta-\gamma\\\alpha&=(180^\circ-\theta)+x\\\alpha&=(180^\circ-\theta)+(\beta-\gamma)\end{align*}$$
